model_params.features: identical 10 per-window time-domain statistics (adapters share window_features); window = 2048 samples in BOTH datasets
model_params.training: fit on ALL paderborn windows of the shared label set; no target data in training

split.protocol: zero-shot cross-dataset transfer: Random Forest trained on all paderborn windows, tested on all cwru windows; label set restricted to the shared ['Normal', 'InnerRace', 'OuterRace']

preprocessing.windowing: non-overlapping 2048-sample windows in both datasets — but the window TIME SPAN differs by sampling rate: 2048 samples = 170.7 ms at CWRU's 12 kHz vs 32.0 ms at Paderborn's 64 kHz
preprocessing.excluded: CWRU 'Ball' class excluded (Paderborn scope has no ball-fault bearing); CWRU windows of that class are dropped from BOTH training (when CWRU is the source) and scoring
preprocessing.scaling: none (tree model on raw time-domain features, as in the in-domain records)

notes: Zero-shot paderborn -> cwru bearing-fault transfer. Known shift factors, all documented rather than corrected: sampling rate 12 kHz (CWRU) vs 64 kHz (Paderborn) so identical 2048-sample windows cover 170.7 ms vs 32.0 ms of shaft rotation; different test rigs, bearing geometries, sensor mounting and load/speed regimes; CWRU faults are EDM-seeded single-point defects, Paderborn's are EDM/drilling/engraving defects on a different bearing type. Time-domain statistics (RMS, kurtosis, ...) are amplitude- and rate-sensitive, so degradation vs the in-domain references is the expected result — this record measures it instead of assuming it.

reference_target_in_domain.protocol: RECORDING-WISE leave-one-recording-out (LeaveOneGroupOut over 12 recordings; groups = recording id): in every fold the held-out recording's windows are the test set and NO window from that recording a
